title: engine: cascade delete runs one id read + one set-based DELETE/UPDATE per relation instead of a full engine write per dependent (epic #33631 R7)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #33631 (SQL performance). Item R7 of the M0 ranked list (#33633): https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/33631#issuecomment-6889544281 (corrected 6889939163). Maintainer's pick (seat decision card, 2026-11-15T06:44Z): 「R1 R7 R12 各一张+测量卡」.

## Today

Cascade delete is one full engine `delete`/`update` per dependent (`engine-cascade-planning.ts` ~1085–1171), each with its hooks, recycle-bin capture and probes: **155 statements** to delete one opportunity with 10 line items (~15 per child), p50 121–237 ms, linear in children.

## Target

Per relation: one id read + one `DELETE … WHERE fk = ?` (or `UPDATE … SET fk = NULL`) + one batched recycle-bin capture, when the child has no per-row hooks. Children with per-row hooks keep today's path. Not yet measured as SQL: the batched capture shape comes first.

## Business reason

Deleting a parent with many children (an order with hundreds of lines) is linear in statements and slow today.

## Reader

domain:server#5 area A4 (engine) with A3 (trash / recycle bin); next account; size M–L.

## Epic rules

- Name the SQL shape produced and give before/after on the M0 bench (`packages/qa/dogfood/bench/sql-perf`, PR #33662).
- Security never regresses: read scope and tenant wall stay in the pushed-down statement, with a parity test against today's path.
- A non-SQL driver keeps an in-process path it already has or refuses with a stable code (epic #33631 rules; #33626 rulings).
